skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: Researchers surveyed a random sample of 500 students at one university and found that students who reported sleeping more hours had higher grades, on average. Which conclusion is best supported?
questions.explanation: A random sample supports conclusions about that university's students, but an observational survey shows only an association, not cause.
choices: Sleeping more causes students at that university to earn higher grades.
Among students at that university, more sleep is associated with higher grades.
More sleep is associated with higher grades for students at every university.
Sleeping more causes all students everywhere to earn higher grades.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A researcher recruited 120 adult volunteers from a city and randomly assigned half of them to drink green tea daily and the other half to drink water daily for 8 weeks. At the end of the study, the green tea group had a lower average blood pressure than the water group. Which conclusion is best supported by the study?
questions.explanation: Random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion, but the volunteers were not a random sample of the city's adults, so the result applies to people like them. The second choice is the trap: random assignment is exactly what allows a causal conclusion.
choices: Drinking green tea daily causes lower blood pressure in all adults in the city.
Green tea is associated with lower blood pressure, but no conclusion about cause can be drawn.
Drinking green tea daily likely caused lower blood pressure among people similar to the volunteers in the study.
Drinking green tea daily lowers blood pressure for people everywhere.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A researcher selected 200 tomato plants of the same variety from one greenhouse and randomly assigned 100 of them to receive a new fertilizer; the other 100 received no fertilizer. The plants that received the fertilizer produced significantly more tomatoes, on average. Which conclusion is best supported by the study?
questions.explanation: Random assignment to the two groups lets the researcher conclude that the fertilizer caused the difference. Because the plants were not randomly selected from all tomato plants, the conclusion applies to plants like these, not to every plant. Random selection affects how widely a result applies, not whether cause can be concluded.
choices: The fertilizer will increase the yield of every tomato plant that receives it.
The fertilizer likely caused an increase in tomato yield for plants like those in the study.
No conclusion about cause is possible, because the 200 plants were not randomly selected from all tomato plants.
The fertilizer will increase the yield of all types of fruit plants.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: Researchers recruited 400 adult volunteers who reported trouble falling asleep. Half of the volunteers, chosen at random, drank a cup of chamomile tea each evening for a month; the others drank a caffeine-free tea that looked and tasted similar but contained no chamomile. On average, the chamomile group fell asleep faster. Which conclusion is best supported by the study?
choices: Drinking chamomile tea likely causes adults with trouble falling asleep, like the volunteers, to fall asleep faster.
Drinking chamomile tea likely causes all adults to fall asleep faster.
Drinking chamomile tea is associated with falling asleep faster, but the study cannot show that it causes faster sleep.
Drinking any kind of tea in the evening likely causes adults to fall asleep faster.
questions.explanation: Random assignment to the two teas supports a cause-and-effect conclusion, so the association-only choice is too weak. But the volunteers were not a random sample of all adults, so the result applies to people like them: adults with trouble falling asleep.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: Researchers selected 500 factory workers at random from all factory workers in a large city. They randomly assigned half of them to a schedule with a 10-minute break every two hours and the other half to their usual schedule. After one month, the workers on the break schedule produced significantly more per hour, on average. Which conclusion is best supported by the study?
questions.explanation: Random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion, and random selection lets it extend to factory workers in that city, but not to other industries. The result is an average effect, not a guarantee for every worker.
choices: The break schedule likely causes higher average hourly output among factory workers in that city.
The break schedule likely causes higher average hourly output among workers in every industry.
The study shows only an association between the break schedule and output, not a cause.
The break schedule will raise the hourly output of every factory worker in the city.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A researcher selected 300 students at random from a large university. Half of these students, chosen at random, used a spaced-review study app for one semester, and the other half did not use the app. The students who used the app had a significantly higher average exam score. Which conclusion is best supported by the study?
questions.explanation: Random assignment to use the app or not supports a conclusion about cause, and random selection from one university lets the conclusion extend to that university's students only. The association-only option ignores the random assignment.
choices: Using the app likely causes higher exam scores among students at that university.
Using the app likely causes higher exam scores among all university students in the country.
Using the app is associated with higher exam scores, but the study cannot show that it causes them.
Every student at the university who uses the app will earn a higher exam score.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A researcher randomly assigned 60 tomato plants in a greenhouse to two groups of 30. One group received a new fertilizer, and the other group received the fertilizer usually used in the greenhouse. The plants that received the new fertilizer produced significantly more tomatoes, on average. Which conclusion is best supported by the study?
choices: The new fertilizer is likely to cause an increase in tomato production for plants like those in the study.
The new fertilizer is likely to increase production for all kinds of crops.
The study shows an association between the new fertilizer and tomato production, but it cannot suggest that the fertilizer caused the increase.
The new fertilizer will increase tomato production for every tomato plant it is used on.
questions.explanation: Random assignment to the two fertilizers lets the researcher conclude cause and effect, but only for plants like those studied. It says nothing about other crops, and an average increase doesn't guarantee an increase for every plant.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A researcher recruited 300 volunteers who wanted to improve their sleep. The volunteers were randomly assigned either to read a printed book or to use a phone for 30 minutes before bed. After four weeks, the book group reported significantly better sleep. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Reading a printed book before bed improves sleep for all adults in the country.
For volunteers like those in the study, reading a printed book before bed instead of using a phone likely causes better sleep.
Using a phone before bed has no effect on sleep.
The results cannot support any conclusion because the volunteers were not chosen at random.
questions.explanation: Random assignment allows a cause-and-effect conclusion, but the volunteers were not a random sample of all adults, so the conclusion applies to people like them. Choice D confuses random selection with random assignment.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A researcher surveyed 2,000 adults and found that those who drank tea every day had, on average, lower blood pressure than those who did not. Which conclusion is best supported by this study?
choices: Drinking tea every day causes lower blood pressure.
People with high blood pressure should start drinking tea.
Among the adults surveyed, daily tea drinking was associated with lower blood pressure.
Tea has no effect on blood pressure.
questions.explanation: This is an observational study: participants were not randomly assigned to drink tea, so it shows an association, not cause and effect. Choices A and B assume a causal link, and choice D contradicts the data.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: Researchers recruited 200 volunteers with mild insomnia and randomly assigned half of them to listen to calming music before bed for one month; the other half did not. On average, the volunteers in the music group fell asleep significantly faster than those in the other group. Which of the following conclusions is best supported by the study?
choices: Listening to calming music before bed causes all people to fall asleep faster.
Listening to calming music before bed is associated with falling asleep faster, but a cause-and-effect relationship cannot be concluded.
Listening to calming music before bed likely causes people with mild insomnia who are similar to the volunteers to fall asleep faster.
Listening to calming music before bed causes people without insomnia to fall asleep faster.
questions.explanation: Random assignment allows a cause-and-effect conclusion, so B is too weak. But the volunteers were not a random sample of everyone, so the result applies only to people like them: those with mild insomnia, not "all people" (A) or people without insomnia (D).

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A researcher randomly selected $500$ adults from a city and randomly assigned half of them to walk $30$ minutes a day for $3$ months while the other half kept their usual routine. The walking group showed a significantly greater decrease in average blood pressure. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Walking $30$ minutes a day causes lower blood pressure for all adults in the world.
For adults in this city, walking $30$ minutes a day is likely to cause a decrease in blood pressure.
There is no relationship between walking and blood pressure.
Adults who choose to walk daily have lower blood pressure, but walking does not cause the decrease.
questions.explanation: Random assignment allows a cause-and-effect conclusion, and random selection from the city allows generalizing to that city's adults, but not to all adults everywhere (A).

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: Researchers randomly assigned $100$ adult volunteers to two groups. One group used a new relaxation app every night for a month, and the other group did not. On average, the group that used the app slept $25$ minutes more per night. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
choices: The app is likely to increase nightly sleep for adults similar to the volunteers.
The app will increase nightly sleep for every adult who uses it.
The app is likely to increase nightly sleep for all people, including children.
No conclusion can be drawn, because the volunteers were not selected at random from all adults.
questions.explanation: Random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion, but the volunteers weren't a random sample of all people. So the conclusion applies to adults like the volunteers, not to everyone (B, C).

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A researcher surveyed $150$ people at a gym and found that most of them exercise at least $4$ days per week. Which of the following is the best reason why the results of this survey should not be used to describe the exercise habits of all adults in the city where the gym is located?
choices: The sample size was too large.
The people surveyed were not selected at random from all adults in the city.
The researcher should have asked about the number of hours exercised instead of days.
Most people do not exercise at gyms.
questions.explanation: People at a gym are likely to exercise more than typical adults, so the sample doesn't represent all adults in the city. A random sample of all adults would be needed.
